rv.q: This delightful American show, set in Memphis in 1955, pins down a pivotal moment in musical history with liberal gaiety. It is propelled as much byJoe DiPietro's book as by the pounding scoreofDavid Bryan, a founder memberofBon Jovi. The show's story is relatively simple.

The UK production's star draw is "British soul queen" Beverley Knight. Hervoice is so extraordinary-seemingly containing the force ofablast furnace - that were she signed to dojustonenumber, this would still be an event.

Soul queen Beverley Knight has first billing as Felicia, and rightly so given her magnificent voice, but the narrative focus is on Huey. Killian Donnelly has all the requisite energy and wackiness, but too much nose and 21st- century phrasing in his singing voice.
It's apluckyproducerwho launches a bignewWest End musical that is neitherbased on a film nor stuffed with old hits.
